newsitem.title: USA: Bankamerica cuts 3,700 jobs, takes $280 million charge.
newsitem.headline: Bankamerica cuts 3,700 jobs, takes $280 million charge.

text.p: Almost one year to the day since he took the helm at BankAmerica Corp., Chief Executive David Coulter on Thursday announced a major restructuring, including the elimination of 3,700 jobs worldwide.
The nation's third largest bank said that as a result of the sweeping restructuring it will take a pre-tax charge of $280 million, resulting in a $165 million reduction in fourth-quarter net income.

"We are changing our business mix in both Europe and Japan based on changing markets and we are streamlining our operations activities around the world," said Coulter, who became chief executive officer last Jan. 1.
"Coulter's focused heavily on rationalisation of business lines. It's ongoing and I expect there'll be more cutbacks," said George Salem of Gerard Klauer Mattison.
"I think this move really brings out Coulter as a very methodical chief executive officer," Salem said.
Since becoming CEO Coulter has said he was taking a hard look at the bank's business lines to determine which divisions were providing adequate returns.
Tom Theurkauf of Keefe Bruyette Woods said the bank's Hawaiian operations might be next in line for some finetuning.
"There are other parts of the bank under scrutiny, such as its Hawaiian operations. While the economy is returning there, the operation has substandard returns," Theurkauf said.
Salem raised his 1997 fiscal year earnings estimate by 10 cents to $8.40 a share. Last year, BankAmerica reported net income of $6.49 a share, or $2.66 billion.
Others were reviewing their estimates.
"Our estimates are under review. I think we're going to raise them, predicated on the cost reductions," said Theurkauf. "And I wouldn't rule out further share repurchases," he said.
Coulter said he expected almost all of the restructuring would be accomplished in 1997, and that the charge will be recovered in cost savings by the end of 1998.
He said BankAmerica will reduce staff and restructure units in mature European markets while expanding activities in emerging European markets.

"The wholesale bank has been under scrutiny. The largest part of the charge is relating to that, particularly in Japan and Europe. It has a reasonable net income but its return on allocated equity has been quite low," said Theurfkauf.
In Japan, the charge relates to a previously announced restructuring of Tokyo's activities and anticipated staff cuts caused by reduced demand for traditional credit products.

The company also said it will close about 120 branches in California during 1997 while adding to other retail services. The bank currently operates about 1,400 retail outlets, as well as 3,800 ATMs, in the state.

"Eliminating positions is always difficult," Coulter said. "However, we have learned that it is better to take such action when the company is performing well, as BankAmerica is today. For instance, the likelihood of placing employees in other positions is better in good circumstances."
The job cuts amount to about 5 percent of BankAmerica's 78,300 employees.
Excluding a one-time Saving Association Insurance Fund (SAIF) assessment, BankAmerica's net income for the first nine months of 1996 was $5.51 a share, or $2.17 billion.
Total assets totalled $243 billion as of the end of September.
BankAmerica's stock lost $2.875 to $94.375 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
